emergency.note: Unified 911 covers Riyadh; legacy numbers 999 (police) and 997 (ambulance) still work, and English-speaking operators are generally available.

hood_landmark.Olaya: Kingdom Centre Tower and its Sky Bridge viewpoint
hood_landmark.Al Malaz: Riyadh Zoo and the historic Al Malaz (Prince Faisal bin Fahd) Stadium
hood_landmark.Diplomatic Quarter: Tuwaiq Palace amid the quarter's landscaped parks and Wadi Hanifah-edge trails
hood_landmark.Al Nakheel: Leafy district beside King Saud University's landmark campus
hood_landmark.King Abdullah Financial District: Futuristic skyscraper cluster around the crystalline KAFD Grand Mosque

avoid.reason: Crime is very low; the real cautions are aggressive driving and strict local laws — avoid photographing government buildings or people without permission.

hood_desc: Riyadh's modern commercial heart along Olaya and Tahlia streets, with skyscrapers like the Kingdom Centre, hotels, malls and restaurants; suits business travelers and first-timers wanting central buzz.
An older, established central district on the original grid, with government offices, stadiums and affordable dining; suits budget travelers and those wanting an authentic, less glossy Riyadh.
A gated, leafy enclave of embassies west of the center, green, secure and low-rise; suits diplomats and those seeking calm, upscale, walkable surroundings.
An affluent modern northern residential district near business hubs, with villas and malls; suits families and long-stay visitors wanting newer, upscale housing.
A gleaming new business megaproject of towers and skybridges in the north with its own metro station; suits business visitors and those wanting cutting-edge modern surroundings.
lodging: Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh at Kingdom Centre

water.note: Treated water meets standards, but bottled water is recommended, especially outside modern hotels.

transit.pay: Use the rechargeable Darb card, tapped at turnstiles for both Metro and Riyadh Bus; buy/load it at station vending machines or the Darb app (contactless bank cards are not yet accepted for entry). Flat fare is about SAR 4 (~$1.07) per trip, with free transfers within a set window.
transit.hours: Metro and buses run roughly 5:30am-midnight Saturday-Wednesday, later on Thursday, and from early afternoon on Friday; there is no overnight service.
